subject: System Design
title: What Is a Cache
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: What Is a Cache.

hook.text: A database query takes 200ms. The same query cached in memory returns in 1ms. That's the power of caching.

buildup.text: A cache stores frequently accessed data in a faster storage layer, reducing the need to fetch from the source.

discovery.text: CPU caches, browser caches, CDN caches, and Redis all apply the same principle at different layers.

twist.text: Caches introduce stale data. The cached version might not match the source. Consistency is the trade-off.

climax.text: Caching is the single most impactful performance optimization in system design.

punchline.text: Store it closer, serve it faster.

quiz.question: What is the main trade-off of caching?
